summary: Afrobeats (modern Nigerian/Ghanaian afropop, Wizkid, Burna Boy, Davido, Rema): 100-115 BPM, a syncopated punchy kick, a rim or clap backbeat and swung 16th shakers with congas, a warm round bass bouncing on the roots (or a log drum), 7th/9th chords on Rhodes or a highlife guitar, a marimba or pluck hook; not Fela's afrobeat (genre/afrobeat); knowledge/style/afrobeats.json is its template
body: Tempo 100-115 BPM (95-115 in some guides); amapiano-flavoured tracks sit at the top.

Drums: a punchy, not very sub-heavy kick, syncopated (often the 3-3-2 of the tresillo) rather than four on the floor; a rimshot or a layered clap on the backbeat, sometimes off the grid; continuous 16th shakers and hats swung 8-20%; congas, bongos, talking drum or woodblock in interlocking call-and-response. Electronic and traditional drums mixed; a small, well-chosen kit grooves better than many sounds.

Bass: melodic and bouncy, a rounded sine or warm bass (closer to a bass guitar than a trap 808) on the roots and fifths, moving with the kick; or a pitched log drum (from amapiano) bouncing between two or three notes, answering the kick, short decay.

Harmony: simple 4- or 8-bar loops, major for upbeat songs (I-V-vi-IV) or minor for emotional ones, coloured with 7ths, 9ths and sus chords; warm electric piano or bell pads held under, clean or palm-muted highlife guitar lines; everything locked to one key.
Lead: a plucked synth, marimba or kalimba hook (short and looping); sax lines on some; smooth stacked vocals carry the song.
Texture/master: clean, punchy and warm: crisp percussion (compressed together on a bus), a tight low end, tasteful reverb and delay; saturation to round it out.

Sources (2026-11-26): Violet Recording 'How to make afrobeats'; Soundtrap 'Beatmaking guide: the history of, and how to make afrobeats'; Splice 'How to make Afrobeat music: Iss 814's walkthrough'; Audeobox 'How to make afrobeats in FL Studio'.
Apply: pattern/gmd-afrobeat-beat-1 on the drums, then pattern/pop-i-v-vi-iv on the keys four bars later. For a whole style change the Team Lead's restyle uses knowledge/style/afrobeats.json instead.

drums.about: the drum track (a kit); leave out if there isn't one

keys.about: a chordal part (keys, pad); leave out if there isn't one

key.about: the project's key; leave out to estimate it from the notes
